doc_description: A synthetic retrieval-benchmark colocation agreement, effective 15 February 2027, between Cedar Peak Infrastructure LLC and Glasshaven Analytics Inc. for twelve racks and 96 kW in Suite D-14 of Building DC-2 at the Cedar Peak Data Campus in Briarfield, Colorado, covering a 36-month term, fees, service levels, security, and Colorado governing law.

structure.title: Agreement, Parties and Effective Date
structure.summary: This Colocation and Managed Facilities Agreement, effective 15 February 2027, is between Cedar Peak Infrastructure LLC (Provider), which operates the Cedar Peak Data Campus in Briarfield, Colorado, and Glasshaven Analytics Inc. (Customer), which needs a managed environment for production analytics. It sets the contract hierarchy: a signed change order controls only its specific subject, followed by the order form, the agreement and the schedules, and marketing descriptions do not vary express commitments. It names operational and contractual contacts for each party, and states that a contact change does not amend obligations. It grants a non-lease contractual license to Suite D-14 in Building DC-2, with twelve racks of nominal 42 rack units each, subject to installation and clearance rules. It commits 96 kW aggregate power with dual A/B feeds, allows up to four diverse carrier cross-connects by signed order, and states that reserving a port activates nothing. Provider controls common areas, while Customer may work only in its allocated racks and may not expand without written authorization. The document is marked as a synthetic retrieval benchmark, not for execution.

structure.title: Licensed Space and Authorized Equipment
structure.summary: This data center colocation agreement for Cedar Peak Data Campus, Building DC-2, grants a contractual license (not a lease) to use Suite D-14, with twelve secured racks of 42 rack units each. The suite has a committed 96 kW aggregate power allocation on dual A/B feeds. The customer may order up to four diverse carrier cross-connects by signed order, and reserving a port does not activate one. The provider controls corridors, mechanical rooms, meet-me rooms and emergency exits. The customer may install or remove listed equipment only in its allocated racks and may not expand into neighboring cabinets without written authorization. The initial 36-month term runs from 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2030, with an acceptance checklist covering power-feed, rack-lock and network-handoff readiness. After the Ready for Service notice, the customer has five Business Days to report material deficiencies in writing, otherwise the service is deemed accepted. One 24-month renewal requires at least 120 calendar days' notice and is priced at list less an 8 percent discount unless a signed order states otherwise. Footers label the text a synthetic retrieval benchmark, not for execution.

structure.title: Term, Acceptance and Renewal
structure.summary: This Data Center Colocation and Managed Facilities Agreement for Cedar Peak Data Campus, Building DC-2, covers term, acceptance, renewal, fees, billing and security. The initial term is 36 months, from the Service Commencement Date of 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2030, with an acceptance checklist for power-feed, rack-lock and network-handoff readiness. After the Provider issues a Ready for Service notice, the Customer has five Business Days to test the configuration and report material deficiencies in writing; otherwise the service is deemed accepted. The Customer may renew once for 24 months with at least 120 calendar days' written notice, at the current list price less an 8 percent discount unless a signed order says otherwise. The monthly colocation license charge is USD 18,600, including twelve racks and up to 96 kW of reserved power. Electricity is billed separately at USD 0.14 per kWh, and cross-connects cost USD 175 each per month. Invoices are issued on the first Business Day of each month, payable net 30. A refundable USD 37,200 security deposit is required and may be applied to undisputed overdue charges after written notice and a ten-day cure period. From 1 April 2028 the license charge rises 3 percent on each anniversary. Power rates change only with 60 days' notice and documented energy cost changes.

structure.title: Fees, Billing and Security
structure.summary: This excerpt from a data center colocation agreement for Cedar Peak Data Campus, Building DC-2, covers fees, payment terms, and service levels. The monthly colocation license is USD 18,600, including twelve racks and up to 96 kW of reserved power. Metered electricity is billed separately at USD 0.14 per kWh, and cross-connects cost USD 175 each per month. Invoices are issued on the first business day of each month, payable net 30. A refundable USD 37,200 security deposit may be applied to undisputed overdue charges after written notice and a ten-day cure period. From 1 April 2028, the license charge rises 3 percent on each service anniversary, and power rates change only with 60 days' notice and documented energy cost changes. The availability target is 99.95 percent monthly for contracted power at the rack PDU demarcation, with exclusions for approved maintenance. A complete loss of both power feeds is Severity 1 with a 15-minute acknowledgement; single-feed degradation is Severity 2 with a 60-minute acknowledgement. Credits of 2 percent of the monthly license charge apply per full 30 minutes of qualifying downtime beyond the allowance, capped at 20 percent, and claims are due within 20 calendar days. The pages are footed as a synthetic retrieval benchmark, not for execution.

structure.title: Service Levels and Outage Credits
structure.summary: This data center colocation agreement for Cedar Peak Data Campus, Building DC-2, covers service levels, outage credits, and physical security. Provider commits to 99.95 percent monthly availability of contracted power at the rack PDU demarcation point, excluding approved scheduled maintenance and listed exclusions. A complete loss of both A and B feeds is Severity 1, requiring engineer acknowledgement within 15 minutes; single-feed degradation is Severity 2, requiring acknowledgement within 60 minutes. For each full 30 minutes of qualifying unavailability beyond allowed downtime, Customer receives a credit of 2 percent of the monthly license charge, capped at 20 percent per month, and must claim it within 20 calendar days. Provider maintains continuous CCTV, badge logs, and a staffed security desk, retaining recordings at least 90 days unless preserved for an incident or legal hold. Customer may nominate up to eight named technicians for unescorted access to Suite D-14; other visitors need 24 hours' advance registration and escort. Provider must notify Customer within four hours of confirming unauthorized physical access to cabinets, identifying scope, containment actions, and an incident coordinator, without unsupported root-cause claims. Pages are footered as a synthetic retrieval benchmark, not for execution.

structure.title: Physical Security and Visitor Controls
structure.summary: This excerpt from a Data Center Colocation and Managed Facilities Agreement for Cedar Peak Data Campus, Building DC-2, covers pages 6 and 7 of 10. Section 6 (Physical Security and Visitor Controls) requires continuous CCTV of common corridors, badge access logs and a staffed security desk, with recordings kept at least 90 days unless preserved longer for an incident or legal hold. Customer may nominate up to eight named technicians for unescorted access to Suite D-14; other visitors need 24 hours' advance registration and escort. Provider must notify Customer within four hours of confirming unauthorized physical access to Customer cabinets, stating known scope, containment actions and the incident coordinator. Section 7 (Maintenance, Change Windows and Remote Hands) schedules routine maintenance on Sundays 02:00 to 06:00 Mountain Time with at least seven days' notice, allowing emergency maintenance to prevent damage or safety risk. Provider includes eight remote-hands hours per month; extra approved assistance costs USD 110 per hour in 15-minute increments with a one-hour minimum per request. Customer must submit a method statement 48 hours before changes affecting cabling, power draw or rack footprint, and Provider may reject changes that threaten cooling, fire protection or neighbors. Both pages are labeled as a synthetic retrieval benchmark, not for execution.

structure.title: Maintenance, Change Windows and Remote Hands
structure.summary: This data center colocation agreement for Cedar Peak Data Campus, Building DC-2, covers maintenance, remote hands, change control, and data responsibility. Routine maintenance that may affect service is scheduled for Sundays 02:00-06:00 Mountain Time with at least seven calendar days' notice, and emergency maintenance may occur outside that window to prevent imminent equipment damage or safety risk. The provider includes eight hours of remote-hands assistance per calendar month; additional approved assistance costs USD 110 per hour in 15-minute increments, with a one-hour minimum per discrete request. Customers must submit a method statement 48 hours before changes that materially alter cabling, power draw, or rack footprint, and the provider may reject changes that reasonably threaten cooling, fire protection, or neighboring customers. The customer retains ownership and control of its applications and data, the provider does not gain inspection rights by hosting the equipment, and the provider does not supply application backup. Confidentiality duties limit use of information to performing the agreement and last three years after expiration, with trade secrets protected while they qualify. Compelled disclosures are allowed only as legally required, with advance notice where permitted, and access credentials may not be shared with subcontractors lacking a documented need to know. The pages are marked as a synthetic retrieval benchmark, not for execution.

structure.title: Data Responsibility and Confidentiality
structure.summary: This section of a data center colocation and managed facilities agreement (Cedar Peak Data Campus, Building DC-2) covers data responsibility, confidentiality, liability, insurance and termination. Customer keeps ownership and operational control of its applications and stored data, and Provider gets no right to inspect Customer content just because the equipment sits on Provider premises. Provider manages building-level services and does not provide application backup. Each Party may use the other's Confidential Information only to perform the agreement and must protect it with at least reasonable care. Ordinary confidentiality obligations survive three years after expiration, while trade secrets stay protected as long as they qualify under law. Compelled legal disclosure is allowed only to the extent required, with prompt advance notice where permitted. Access credentials may not go to subcontractors without a documented need to know. Liability is capped at twelve months of recurring license charges, except for fraud, willful misconduct, unpaid fees and confidentiality breaches. Provider must carry USD 2 million per-occurrence general liability and USD 5 million aggregate cyber insurance, while Customer insures its own hardware. Either Party may terminate for material breach uncured 30 days after written notice, and nonpayment of undisputed invoices has a separate 15-day cure period. Both pages are marked as a synthetic contract for retrieval benchmarking and not for execution.

structure.title: Liability, Insurance and Termination
structure.summary: This synthetic data center colocation and managed facilities agreement for Cedar Peak Data Campus, Building DC-2 (marked as a retrieval benchmark, not for execution) covers liability, insurance, termination, and exit terms. Liability is capped at twelve months of recurring license charges paid or payable before the claim, excluding fraud, willful misconduct, unpaid fees, and confidentiality breaches. The Provider must carry USD 2 million per-occurrence general liability and USD 5 million aggregate cyber insurance, while the Customer insures its own equipment. Either party may terminate for material breach uncured 30 days after written notice; nonpayment of undisputed invoices has a separate 15-day cure period. Customer must remove equipment within 20 Business Days after service ends and restore racks, with supervised access and possible storage fees. Formal notices require overnight courier or tracked registered mail, with email as a courtesy copy; tickets and email alone are not valid termination notices. Colorado law governs, with exclusive venue in Denver courts and urgent injunctive relief permitted.

structure.title: Exit, Notices and Governing Law
structure.summary: This excerpt from a data center colocation and managed facilities agreement for Cedar Peak Data Campus, Building DC-2, covers exit, notices and governing law. Under equipment removal, the customer must remove its equipment within 20 Business Days after service ends and restore racks to a safe, clean condition. The provider offers supervised access for this and may charge reasonable documented storage fees after the removal period. Under formal notices, notices must be sent by recognized overnight courier or tracked registered mail to the legal addresses in the order form, with an email courtesy copy. Operational tickets and email alone are not valid termination notices. Under governing law, the agreement is governed by Colorado law without regard to conflict-of-laws principles. Exclusive venue for contractual disputes is the state or federal courts in Denver, Colorado, and the parties may seek urgent injunctive relief where legally appropriate. The footer marks the document as a synthetic contract for retrieval benchmarking, not for execution, on page 10 of 10.
